  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],

  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) for each of the five response variables separately, with Stimulation Paradigm as the independent factor.",
    "For Time-to-Target, Average Speed, and AD (continuous variables): Use standard One-Way ANOVA to test H0: mu_Combined = mu_ICMS = mu_Dim = mu_Bright = mu_Sham.",
    "For Success (binary variable): Use One-Way ANOVA as an approximation for large sample sizes (n > 3000 per group), noting that Chi-Square tests or Logistic Regression with fixed effects are theoretically more appropriate for binary outcomes, but proceeding with ANOVA per the requested workflow structure for this specific variable.",
    "For Path Efficiency (continuous, bounded 0-1): Use One-Way ANOVA, checking for normality and homoscedasticity given the bounded nature of the data.",
    "Report F-statistics, degrees of freedom, and p-values for each model."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA yields a significant main effect (p < 0.05), conduct post-hoc pairwise comparisons between all five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Use Tukey's Honest Significant Difference (HSD) test for all continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "For the Success variable, if ANOVA is significant, use pairwise t-tests with Bonferroni correction or contrast analysis to identify specific differences between paradigms.",
    "Report mean differences, 95% confidence intervals, and adjusted p-values for all significant pairwise comparisons."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Apply Tukey's Honest Significant Difference (HSD) correction for continuous response variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) to maintain the family-wise error rate at alpha=0.05 across all pairwise comparisons. For the binary Success variable, apply Bonferroni correction to pairwise t-tests if post-hoc analysis is deemed necessary.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Do not use ordinary linear regression for Success as it violates assumptions for binary outcomes. Instead, recommend a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with a binomial link function (Logistic Regression) where Stimulation Paradigm is a categorical fixed effect and Success is the response. For the four continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD), a standard One-Way ANOVA (equivalent to linear regression with categorical dummy variables) is appropriate, provided normality and homoscedasticity assumptions are met. If residuals show severe non-normality or heteroscedasticity, consider a Generalized Linear Model with a Gamma distribution and log link for skewed positive data (Time-to-Target, Average Speed) or a Beta regression for bounded data (Path Efficiency, AD).",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Assumed based on experimental design (different mice or trials), but should be verified by checking for repeated measures within mice if data structure allows.",
    "Normality of residuals: Must be checked for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; transformations (e.g., log) may be required for skewed distributions.",
    "Homogeneity of variances (Homoscedasticity): Must be checked using Levene's test or Bartlett's test across the five stimulation groups for all continuous variables.",
    "Linearity: Not applicable for ANOVA, but relevant if extending to GLMs.",
    "For Success variable: Check for separation issues and verify that the large sample size justifies the normal approximation used in ANOVA for binary data."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on descriptive statistics, the Sham group is expected to show significantly lower Success rates (0.27) and higher Time-to-Target (4.68s) compared to other groups, indicating impaired navigation.",
    "The Combined group is expected to show the highest Path Efficiency (0.50) and Average Speed (12.83), suggesting synergistic effects of stimulation.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to be lowest in the Dim Visual Only group (0.34) compared to Sham (0.24) and Combined (0.40), though the difference may not be statistically significant without formal testing.",
    "Significant main effects of Stimulation Paradigm are expected for Time-to-Target, Success, and Average Speed given the large effect sizes observed in the summary data.",
    "Path Efficiency and AD may show significant differences, particularly between Sham and Combined, but variance may be higher, requiring careful post-hoc interpretation."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The Success variable is binary; using ANOVA is an approximation that relies on the Central Limit Theorem due to large sample sizes, but GLMs are theoretically superior.",
    "Path Efficiency and AD are bounded variables (0 to 1 or 0 to 29.8); standard ANOVA assumes unbounded normal distributions, which may be violated, especially near boundaries.",
    "Time-to-Target is heavily skewed (mean 2.8, max 201.4); normality assumptions for ANOVA may require log-transformation.",
    "Potential confounding variables such as individual mouse differences (8 levels of Mouse) are not included in the one-way ANOVA model, which could inflate error variance and reduce statistical power.",
    "The 'Combined' group has a much larger sample size (n=48846) compared to others, which may lead to over-representation of this condition in statistical tests."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a Mixed-Effects Model (Linear Mixed Model for continuous variables, GLMM for Success) with Stimulation Paradigm as a fixed effect and Mouse ID as a random intercept to account for within-mouse correlation and potential confounding effects of individual animal variability. Additionally, perform residual diagnostics for the ANOVA models to determine if transformations (e.g., log for Time-to-Target, Box-Cox for others) are necessary to meet normality and homoscedasticity assumptions."
}
